tools.name: how_aevum_works
tools.description: Rules, call types, supported assets, windows, costs and limits for locking and grading calls on Aevum. Call this first if unsure what can be locked.

tools.name: get_record
tools.description: The public Aevum record of an Ethereum wallet (person, bot or AI agent): every call it locked with status (running, verified, abandoned), result (correct/wrong/void), certificate ids, and summary counts. Use for 'is this trader/agent any good?' or 'show me 0x...'s record'.

tools.name: get_certificate
tools.description: One graded call's certificate, read from Ethereum: the attestation note (grade, prices), return in basis points, the locked call text when public, timestamps and links.

tools.name: recheck_certificate
tools.description: Independently re-grade a certificate: fetches the public prices (Atlas on-chain, Coinbase candles, or Kraken trades), applies the locked rule with the grader's own open code, and compares with what Aevum recorded on Ethereum. Returns match / mismatch / unsupported with each step. Takes a few seconds

tools.name: draft_call
tools.description: Prepare a market call. Always returns a link where a person reviews and locks it in their own wallet (Aevum never signs for anyone). If `address` is given, also returns the exact call text and unsigned Ethereum transactions, for an agent that signs with its own wallet and then calls publish_call. Ty

tools.name: register_agent
tools.description: Give an AI agent a public identity card on Aevum, written on Ethereum by the agent's own wallet (only that wallet can create or change it; each change becomes a dated version, and calls on the record show which version made them). Without `address`: returns a link where the operator connects the age

tools.name: publish_agent_card
tools.description: After the agent's wallet sent the register/update transaction from register_agent and it is mined: submit the transaction hash. Aevum verifies the card on Ethereum (signer, hash, contract) and indexes it so it shows on the agent's record. Safe to repeat.

tools.name: get_agent
tools.description: An AI agent's verified identity card (name, operator, website, framework, model, version...), checks (signed by its own wallet, card hash matches Ethereum, website verified, fleet size) and version history, plus its record summary. Use for 'who is this agent?' or 'is this agent's name real?'.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: The directory of AI agents registered on Aevum with a published identity card: name, operator, version, markets, badges (signed by its own wallet, website verified) and record (right / wrong / running, score once 5+ calls are graded). Use for 'which AI trading agents have a verified record?' or to c

tools.name: publish_call
tools.description: After an agent's own wallet has sent the lock transaction from draft_call and it is mined: submit the transaction hash and the exact call text. Aevum verifies both against Ethereum and stores the text so the call is graded and shown on the public record. Safe to repeat.

tools.name: check_polymarket_wallet
tools.description: A Polymarket wallet's highlight vs its whole record, from Polymarket's own public data: this week / 30 days / all-time results and ranks, max drawdown, and stats over resolved positions (hit rate, average win vs loss, biggest win and loss, how much of the profit came from the top 3 markets). Use for

tools.name: check_payout_wallet
tools.description: Stablecoin payouts a wallet has actually sent, from public block explorers: total, number of transfers, median and largest, how many different wallets received them, repeat recipients, how concentrated they are, the last 30 days, month by month for a year, and days since the last transfer. Built for

tools.name: prove_it_message
tools.description: Writes a short, polite message a buyer can send a signal seller (Discord, Telegram, X, email) asking them to lock their next calls on Aevum before the buyer pays, so wins and losses both end up on a record anyone can check. Nothing is sent or stored; return the text for the person to copy.

tools.name: check_hyperliquid_wallet
tools.description: A Hyperliquid wallet's highlight vs its whole record, from Hyperliquid's own public data: this week / 30 days / all-time P&L, how it did before this month, max drawdown, account value, and stats over recent closed trades (win rate, average win vs loss, worst trade). Use when someone shares a hot Hyp

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "draft_call" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: prove_it_message · Private data: get_record, draft_call, register_agent, publish_agent_card, get_agent, list_agents, publish_call, check_polymarket_wallet, check_payout_wallet, prove_it_message, check_hyperliquid_wallet · Public sink: publish_agent_card, publish_call, prove_it_message · Destructive: recheck_certificate.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: prove_it_message · Private data: get_record, draft_call, register_agent, publish_agent_card, get_agent, list_agents, publish_call, check_polymarket_wallet, check_payout_wallet, prove_it_message, check_hyperliquid_wallet · Public sink: publish_agent_card, publish_call, prove_it_message · Destructive: recheck_certificate

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
